blocks.value: A repetition operator applies to **the item immediately before it**: one character, one bracket group, or one parenthesised group.
Regular expressions allow powerful validation without much code:

The dot represents any character and the asterisk any number of occurrences of the item preceding it, so `".*"` means **any number of any characters**: it matches everything, including the empty string.
That is: an optional single character of any kind, followed by exactly ten digits in the range 0–5.

public class RegexBasics {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println("cat".matches("cat|dog"));        // true
        System.out.println("Dog".matches("[Cc]at|[Dd]og"));  // true
        System.out.println("dOg".matches("[Cc]at|[Dd]og"));  // false
        System.out.println("bat".matches("[a-z]at"));        // true
        System.out.println("Bat".matches("[a-z]at"));        // false
        System.out.println("7x".matches("[0-9]."));          // true
        System.out.println("AAAAAAA".matches("A{7}"));       // true
        System.out.println("AAAA".matches("A{5,}"));         // false
        System.out.println("0912345678".matches("\\d{10}")); // true
        System.out.println("my cat".matches("cat"));         // false, whole string only
    }
}
